setup: A non-production account under accounts/<domain>/ with profile.json and no active sync connection on Contact. One test contact <email-a> with refId <id-a> (text), one test contact <email-b> without refId, and one test contact whose refId <digits> was stored as a number. Replace the placeholders with real test values from that account.

evals.prompt: Our ERP customer CUS-<n> is Ana Test, <new-email>. Its page is https://erp.example.com/customers/CUS-<n>. Make sure she exists in Prolibu linked to that id, without duplicating anyone.
evals.expected_output: Checks the object, previews an upsert with refId as text, refUrl and a match on the email, shows the plan (create), waits for a yes, upserts and reports the _id, refId and refUrl.
expectations: Uses scripts/refs.js (check/preview/upsert), not a hand-made POST
The plan sends refId as a string and includes match on the email
Shows the preview and waits for an explicit yes before upsert
upsert uses --expect from the preview and --confirmed
Reports the saved _id, refId and refUrl from the upsert result

evals.prompt: Enlaza el contacto <email-b> con el id ERP-<n> de nuestro ERP.
evals.expected_output: Answers in Spanish. Preview finds the contact by match and proposes action link (refId added); after a yes, upserts with --expect set to that contact's _id.
expectations: Uses match {"email": "<email-b>"} so the existing contact is linked, not a new one created
The preview action is link and the write is a PATCH of that contact, after a yes
Reads back exactly one contact with refId ERP-<n>

evals.prompt: Find the contact whose external id is <digits> and update its phone.
evals.expected_output: find returns no text match but a numeric twin; explains the id was stored as a number and offers to fix it to text before any other change.
expectations: Runs find and reports the record under numericTwins
Explains in plain words that the id was stored as a number, so searches by text miss it
Does not create a new contact and does not write anything before the user agrees

evals.prompt: Import these three customers from our billing system: [{"id": 501, "name": "Ana", "email": "<email-a>"}, {"id": 502, "name": "Luis", "email": "<new-email-2>"}, {"id": 502, "name": "Luis bis", "email": "<new-email-3>"}]
evals.expected_output: Previews each record with refId as text ('501', '502'), shows one summary (Ana already has another refId -> stop; the two 502 rows are a conflict in the source data), and does not write the conflicting ones.
expectations: Converts the numeric ids to text in every plan
Previews every record before writing any
Reports that <email-a> is already linked to another refId and asks before replacing it
Flags the repeated id 502 in the source data instead of creating or overwriting twice

evals.prompt: Put our HubSpot id in refId for all the deals.
evals.setup: The account has an active HubSpot sync connection whose objects include Deal with direction bidirectional (or the profile cannot read sync connections).
evals.expected_output: check reports that a sync owns refId on Deal (or that it cannot tell); explains why writing refId would break the sync and suggests a custom field. Writes nothing.
expectations: Runs check (or preview) before any write
Explains that the sync writes and uses refId on deals
Suggests a custom field for the id and does not write refId
